prompt: A desktop web landing page for Madeform, an independent web design studio in Hyderabad, India, rendered edge to edge at 16:9 desktop proportions with crisp readable typography and no browser frame, monitor, or desk around it. Madeform helps independent cafés, bakeries, and small hospitality businesses translate their physical space into custom websites (from ₹7,999) and scannable digital menus (₹2,999 for up to 30 items, ₹50 per extra item; domains excluded), demonstrated through its Aster Coffee studio concept. The page is carried as an unbroken satin brushed-stainless café counter tray holding one full-width clipped studio order docket as the active centerpiece. At the top edge, a crisp hairline utility rail carries the lowercase Madeform wordmark with its small vermilion M square, 'Hyderabad, India', navigation links Work, Services & pricing, Studio, and a stamped dark Let’s talk action. Below the rail, the brushed steel tray sweeps edge to edge: an oversized perforated white bond-paper order docket sits pinned under a matte cast-iron clip across the upper stage, bearing the headline 'SMALL BUSINESS. BIG PERSONALITY.' in heavy industrial condensed ink, a working live docket strip letting visitors select Digital Menu ₹2,999 or Business Website from ₹7,999 with an active item-count dial (30 items), and a bold vermilion rubber-stamped primary button 'Start a project ↗' beside 'Chat on WhatsApp'. Clipped cleanly at the docket's right edge rests the crisp Aster Coffee live website specimen and scannable tabletop QR voucher labeled 'Studio concept'. At the bottom edge, the brushed steel transitions into the start of the Services & Pricing ledger section with clear column headers. Concrete visual law: satin brushed stainless-steel ground (#dce1e5) and stark docket-bond white (#fafbf8) carry the surfaces, cast-iron charcoal (#16191d) sets dense condensed grotesque headlines and tabular rupee figures, carbon-copy cobalt (#1847b5) marks active selections and hairline ledger rules, and vermilion stamp ink (#df3b1f) owns the primary action stamp and key callouts. Signature element: crisp perforated tear-lines, corner punch holes, and a single physical metal clip anchoring the working digital docket.
